- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6744a8d9e89a850d615039884ef9e746a96494ee` — the merge of head `5cf1aa4ce32c79362b70f9c52d972cba65a9de83` into base `284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6744a8d9e89a850d615039884ef9e746a96494ee && git checkout 6744a8d9e89a850d615039884ef9e746a96494ee
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4 5cf1aa4ce32c79362b70f9c52d972cba65a9de83 && git checkout -B drift-repro 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4 && git merge --no-ff 5cf1aa4ce32c79362b70f9c52d972cba65a9de83

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 284e04810a309d5a7c8c3654b036f9ebf07a53d4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5cf1aa4ce32c79362b70f9c52d972cba65a9de83`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/25245-mcp-stdio-object-resources-merged.md, packages/mcp/README.md, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.merged-object-resources.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-stdio-package-object-discovery.test.ts + packages/mcp/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/package.json, packages/mcp/src/metadata-completeness.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Read against the net diff `0b8bce40e081477132d81b1e11a19cd3cdb331c0..5cf1aa4ce32c79362b70f9c52d972cba65a9de83` (7 files, +495/−31), card #25245 with all three comments, and the head's check-runs. Every claim below is judged against the cited code at the head, not against the PR body.

### ① Derived judgments

**Published declaration surface of `@objectstack/mcp` — unchanged. Right.** `git diff` of `packages/mcp/src/index.ts` and `packages/mcp/package.json` between base and head is empty; the exports map serves only `./dist/index.js` / `./dist/index.d.ts` (and the cjs pair). `McpObjectView` (a picked pair of `listObjects` and `getObject` off `IMetadataService`), `setRuntimeObjectView` and the two builders `buildObjectListResource` / `buildObjectSchemaResource` are `export`ed from `mcp-server-runtime.ts`, and `stdioObjectView` from `stdio-data-bridge.ts`, but none is re-exported by `index.ts`. The only barrel export that touches the new code is the class `MCPServerRuntime`, whose `bridgeResources(metadataService, getRecord?)` keeps its two parameters; the view is looked up inside the method body through a module-level weak map keyed by the runtime instance, which no declaration names. The builders' new optional trailing parameter is therefore not in the published `.d.ts` either. No api-surface snapshot gate exists for this package, so this is judged from the barrel, which is the whole of what tsup bundles.

**The merged view is shared, not a second copy of the merge (the card's ⛔). Right.** One merge implementation remains: `readMergedObjects(reads)` in `stdio-data-bridge.ts`, unchanged from #25243. `stdioObjectView(reads)` wraps it once; `createStdioDataBridge` builds `objectView = stdioObjectView(reads)` and both `listObjects` and `describeObject` now answer through it (their bodies lost their own copies of the fallback logic); `plugin.ts` line 804 hands `stdioObjectView({ metadataService, protocol: protocolReads })` to `setRuntimeObjectView(this.runtime, …)` over the same `metadataService` and the same `protocolReads` accessor the bridge receives at line 730 and the record resource's gate at line 752. Two closures, one function, one accessor.

**Hoisting `protocolReads` in `plugin.ts`. Right.** It moves from inside the stdio branch to `start()` scope immediately after the `mergedRead` block; `ctx` is the `start(ctx)` parameter so the accessor still resolves `ctx.getService('protocol')` at each call; the stdio branch's `createStdioDataBridge` and `gateReads` still reference it; `setRuntimeObjectView` is called under `if (metadataService)` before `bridgeResources`, outside the stdio branch, so the resources carry the view whether or not the transport auto-starts. Order is irrelevant anyway: `bridgeResources` reads `runtimeObjectViews.get(this) ?? metadataService` inside each resource handler, and the arrow captures `this` lexically.

**The numbered Contract list — every input named, each old/new reading right per the code:**

1. `objectstack://objects` on an `environmentId` kernel, boot-registered object: old omitted (no copy in the metadata service), new listed — `readFlattenedMetaItems` starts from `engine.registry.listItems('object')` on both kernel shapes. The resource applies no system-object filter and `list_objects` applies one unless `allowSystemObjects`, so "the non-`sys_` set is what `list_objects` lists" is the correct phrasing, and the dogfood pin compares exactly that set.
2. `objectstack://objects/NAME` on such an object: old `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, new the schema body. Both the builder and `describeObject` map the same definition to `name` / `label` / `fields` as an array of `{ name, type, label, required }` / `enableFeatures: def.enable ?? {}`, so equality to `describe_object`'s body holds field for field.
3. A disabled package's objects where the metadata service still holds a copy (the narrowing): the merged listing omits them at `protocol.ts` line 10616 — the `items` array is filtered to drop every item for which `isItemOfDisabledPackage(this.engine.registry, item)` is true, applied to every type except `package` — and `stdioObjectView.getObject` is a `find` over that same listing, so the miss reaches `diagnoseEmptyRead` with the metadata service healthy and answers the coded `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. The answer is the miss, not `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`: that is what `describe_object` has answered since #25243 (the protocol's by-name read at line 11426 would raise the disabled refusal, and the view deliberately does not use it), while the record resource's gate still goes through `readObjectDeclaration`'s by-name read and keeps raising the refusal for data. That is the card's "keep the exposure gate's reading", kept.
4. A served definition that differs from the copy: follows from reading the registry-plus-overlay merge instead of `metadataService.getObject`.
5. The merged listing throws: `readMergedObjects` has no `catch`, the view has none, the builders `await` it before any verdict, so the rejection leaves the resource handler and the SDK answers a JSON-RPC error. The protocol itself rethrows every overlay-read failure except "sys_metadata not provisioned" (`rethrowUnlessMetadataStoreUnprovisioned`), so on a real store outage this path is reached. Declared in the Contract list and in the changeset's "Also changed" bullet; pinned with a throwing double only, as the PR says.

**Outage / partial verdict unchanged. Right.** `buildObjectListResource` still calls `diagnoseListRead(metadataService, 'object')` (`listDiagnosed`) on every answer and `buildObjectSchemaResource` still calls `diagnoseEmptyRead(metadataService, 'object', name)` (`getDiagnosed`) on a miss; only the items' source changed. This is the same composition the bridge's `listObjectsDiagnosed` uses for `list_objects` (items from `bridge.listObjects()`, verdict from `diagnoseObjectListRead(metadataService)`). One reading to hold onto: "a loader outage still withholds `totalCount`" names the metadata service's loaders; a `sys_metadata` outage inside the protocol is item 5, a throw, not a `partial`. The PR body and changeset state both, consistently.

**Discovery stays ungated. Right.** Neither builder calls `enforceApiExposure`; the `apiEnabled: false` object is listed and described, as `list_objects` / `describe_object` do, and the dogfood pin asserts it.

**Accept-set changes implied by the diff, each named:** (a) the two object resources now accept the merged listing as their item source — correct; (b) a name absent from the merged listing is now refused with the coded miss even where a copy exists — correct, and it is the declared narrowing; (c) a protocol throw now refuses the read instead of answering the copy — correct and declared; (d) a host with no `protocol` service, or one without `getMetaItems`, reads the metadata service byte-identically — correct per `readMergedObjects` returning `undefined` and both view members falling through to `listObjects()` / `getObject(name)`; (e) a host that calls `bridgeResources` on its own runtime reads the metadata service — correct, the weak map is empty for it. Nothing else in the diff moves an accept set.

**What the head's check-runs measured and what they did not.** Test Core (6/6, aggregate `success`) ran `packages/mcp`, so the 14-case unit file ran in CI. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` excludes `@objectstack/dogfood` from the Test Core shards and runs the Dogfood Regression Gate shards only off `pull_request` / `merge_group`; on this head those shards are `skipped` and the always-on gate concluded `success` with zero attestations. So the 10 real-kernel pins in `packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-stdio-package-object-discovery.test.ts`, and the red-before/green-after table built on them, rest on the dev's local verification until `main`'s first full-battery run after landing. The pins themselves read correctly against the code (the `boot` fixture's disabled-package precondition asserts the copy exists on the no-`environmentId` shape, which is exactly the row the narrowing changes).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25245-mcp-stdio-object-resources-merged.md` bumps `'@objectstack/mcp': patch`. The package publishes (no `private` flag, version 18.0.0), so `skip-changeset` would have been wrong and is not used. The diff moves no spec key, authorable spelling, metadata type or stored shape: `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, and per the Post-Task Checklist a non-protocol change, breaking or not, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. Both line-initial declarations, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, are present in the PR body and in the changeset body; the title carries `!`; the BREAKING banner is present and names the narrowing (a disabled package's objects no longer served by the resources). The `(narrowing)` arm is right: a read that was served (the copy of a disabled package's object on the no-`environmentId` shape) is now refused. The claim comments agree after revision 6346855817, which supersedes the bare `Clause-②: no` of 6346581465 with the measured arm.

ADR-0087: exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The changeset's own remedy line is "Nothing", so the category's statement-against-statement check holds; no exported declaration is removed or narrowed (the barrel is unchanged), so the three export categories do not apply; the package is published, so not `unpublished`; no ADR-0087 id is named, so neither `registered` nor `already-registered`. Check Changeset and Lint & Repo Gates are `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Prompt bridge captures the protocol once (#8328).** Confirmed at `plugin.ts` lines 429–446: `mergedRead` is resolved in `start()` and handed to `bridgePrompts`, not re-read per use. Pre-existing, skills not objects, and not measured by this PR. Answered: out of this card's scope and not a blocker; a card in this family is owed only once the lane measures it (a card names its evidence).
2. **`objectstack://objects/NAME` reads the whole merged listing per call.** Same cost profile as `describe_object` since #25243 and the HTTP bridge since #25136; no contract change. Answered: accepted.
3. **File surface wider than the first claim.** Claim revision 6346855817 names `stdio-data-bridge.ts` (the shared view), the README paragraph and the dogfood file; the diff's seven paths match that surface exactly. Answered.
4. **Branch name `claude/project-thread-dkk3hd`.** The "card this PR closes must claim this branch" check is `success`, and the newest `Claim:` on #25245 names this branch. The Duplicate Fix Guard concern is advisory. Answered.
5. **Raised here: the real-kernel pins have not run in CI on this head** (① last paragraph). Escalated as a reading, not a finding: by the two-speed convention the first full-battery run on `main` after landing measures them, and a red there is this lane's main-red.
6. **Check-runs at signing.** The five required contexts — Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard — are all `success`. One advisory check, "Part-of PR must not also close its card", was still `in_progress` (started 2026-10-22T18:26:25Z) on both reads; it is outside the required set and the PR carries one closing keyword, `Fixes #25245`.
7. The PR is a draft. Landing stays with the owning seat after this record; nothing here readies, queues or arms it.
